title: Libyan Independence Proclaimed
reason: Confirmed: December 24, 1951, King Idris proclaimed the United Kingdom of Libya. First African country independent via UN process. All core details correct.

title: Constitution of the United Kingdom of Libya
reason: Confirmed: 1951 constitution established bicameral parliament (Senate + House of Representatives), federal structure across three provinces, Islam as state religion. All details correct.

title: First Libyan General Elections
reason: Confirmed: Elections held February 19, 1952. Pro-king candidates dominated. Minor correction: event says 'February 1952' which is accurate. Description of limited party activity and royal influence is supported.

title: US Wheelus Air Base Agreement Signed
reason: Confirmed: The 1954 base agreement (signed September 9, 1954) is the main formalization granting US use until 1971. An initial 1951 base-rights agreement also existed. The event is dated 1952 but the formal basing agreement was 1954 — minor year discrepancy. Core facts about financial payments and Cold War significance are correct.

title: Petroleum Exploration Concessions Granted
reason: Confirmed: Libya began granting oil exploration concessions from the early 1950s, accelerating with the 1955 Petroleum Law. Preliminary survey activity in 1954 is consistent with historical record.

title: Libyan Petroleum Law Enacted
reason: Confirmed: Libya enacted Petroleum Law No. 25 of 1955, establishing the framework for exploration and production. Provisions dividing concessions among multiple companies and royalty structures are all confirmed.

title: Suez Crisis Resonates in Libya
reason: Confirmed: The 1956 Suez Crisis is a documented historical event that caused anti-Western sentiment across Libya. The monarchy's constrained reaction and radicalization of pan-Arab movements is well-established context.

title: Major Oil Discovery at Zelten Field
reason: Confirmed: Esso made the first commercial oil strike at Zelten in April/June 1959. Discovery well tested at 17,500 bpd. Reserves estimated at 2.5 billion barrels. All core facts correct.

title: Libya Joins OPEC at Founding
reason: FALSE: Libya was NOT a founding member of OPEC. OPEC was founded September 14, 1960 in Baghdad by Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, and Venezuela only. Libya joined OPEC in 1962, two years later.

title: Federal System Abolished, Unitary State Created
reason: Confirmed: King Idris declared end of federalism on April 26, 1963. Law No. 1 of 1963 abolished the federal regime. Three provinces reorganized into ten governorates. All details correct.

title: Six-Day War Triggers Oil Embargo Attempt
reason: Confirmed: Anti-Western protests erupted in Libya after the June 1967 Six-Day War. Mobs attacked Western facilities. Libya temporarily halted oil shipments. The Khartoum Resolution allowed resumption. All core details verified.

title: Gaddafi's Coup Deposes King Idris
reason: Confirmed: September 1, 1969, Free Unionist Officers led by Gaddafi overthrew the monarchy in a bloodless coup while King Idris was in Turkey. RCC established Libyan Arab Republic. All details correct.

title: Revolutionary Command Council Takes Power
reason: Confirmed: RCC with Gaddafi as chairman suspended constitution, dissolved parliament, banned political parties, demanded removal of foreign bases. Received immediate recognition from Egypt and Arab states.

title: US Evacuates Wheelus Air Base
reason: Confirmed: US evacuated Wheelus Air Base on June 11, 1970, following Libyan pressure. Ceremony with US flag lowering attended. Britain also evacuated its Libyan facilities simultaneously. All details correct.

title: Tripoli Agreement on Oil Pricing
reason: Confirmed: The Tripoli Agreement was signed April 2, 1971 (not 1970 as the year field states), raising posted prices significantly and setting a precedent for OPEC negotiations. Year in the event is off by one year.

title: Partial Nationalization of BP Operations
reason: Confirmed: Libya nationalized BP's assets on December 7, 1971 (event filed under 1972 — year is off by one). Retaliation for Britain's failure to prevent Iran seizing Gulf islands. Arabian Gulf Exploration Company created. Core facts correct, year slightly off.

title: Oil Embargo and Nationalization of Remaining Companies
reason: Confirmed: Libya nationalized 51% stakes in international oil companies in September 1973. Libya participated in the oil embargo but as a unique actor (had already nationalized). Oil prices rose sharply. Core facts verified.

title: Green Book Published
reason: Confirmed: Green Book Part 1 published in late 1975, rejecting representative democracy in favor of direct democracy through Basic Popular Congresses. Part 2 (economics) published 1977. Mandatory study confirmed.

title: Jamahiriya Formally Proclaimed
reason: Confirmed: On March 2, 1977, the General People's Congress proclaimed the Great Socialist People's Libyan Arab Jamahiriya at Sebha. Gaddafi held no formal state office. All details correct.

title: Libya-Egypt Border War
reason: Confirmed: Four-day border war from July 21-24, 1977. Artillery and air strikes exchanged. Ceasefire arranged under Algerian/PLO mediation and US pressure. Triggered by Sadat's peace overtures toward Israel. All details correct.

title: Libyan Intervention in Chad Begins
reason: Confirmed: Significant Libyan military engagement in Chad in 1978, supporting GUNT forces. Aouzou Strip occupied from early 1970s. Libya severed diplomatic relations context is correct. Details on disputed 1955 treaty are accurate.

title: Private Business Abolished Under Green Book
reason: Confirmed: In 1978, Green Book's economic prescriptions implemented. Law passed in May 1978 prohibiting rental of premises. People's Committees seized hundreds of businesses in September 1978. Economic disruption and emigration of skilled workers documented.

title: US Embassy in Tripoli Attacked and Burned
reason: Confirmed: December 2, 1979, approximately 2,000 Libyan students sacked and burned the US Embassy in Tripoli. Staff escaped. Libyan government failed to protect the embassy. Relations downgraded. All details correct.

title: Libyan Intelligence Assassinates Dissidents Abroad
reason: Confirmed: Systematic program of assassinations in 1980 in London, Rome, and other European cities. Gaddafi labeled dissidents 'stray dogs'. Multiple confirmed killings in London and Rome documented. All core details correct.

title: Gulf of Sidra Confrontation with US Navy
reason: Confirmed: August 19, 1981, two US F-14s shot down two Libyan Su-22s after Libya fired first. Libya claimed entire Gulf of Sidra as territorial waters. First Navy air combat since Vietnam War. All details correct.

title: US Designates Libya State Sponsor of Terrorism
reason: FALSE: Libya was placed on the US state sponsors of terrorism list on December 29, 1979, not 1981. It was part of the first such list ever published. The event year is wrong by two years.

title: France Intervenes in Chad Against Libya
reason: Confirmed: France launched Operation Manta in August 1983, deploying up to 2,700 troops to support Habré government against Libyan/GUNT forces. Halted Libyan advances. 15th parallel Red Line established. All details correct.

title: UK Breaks Diplomatic Relations After Embassy Shooting
reason: Confirmed: WPC Yvonne Fletcher shot dead outside Libyan People's Bureau on April 17, 1984. UK broke diplomatic relations on April 22, 1984. Severance lasted eleven years. All details correct.

title: US Sanctions Expanded on Libya
reason: Confirmed: Reagan expanded sanctions against Libya in 1985, with comprehensive embargo announced January 1986 following December 1985 airport attacks. US oil companies were given deadlines. Core facts correct though the comprehensive embargo technically came January 1986.

title: Rome and Vienna Airport Attacks
reason: Confirmed: December 27, 1985 attacks at Rome Fiumicino and Vienna Schwechat airports. 19 people killed (including one child), ~140 wounded. Abu Nidal Organization responsible with Libyan intelligence support confirmed. All details correct.

title: US Bombing of Libya: Operation El Dorado Canyon
reason: Confirmed: April 15, 1986, US struck Tripoli and Benghazi including Bab al-Azizia compound. Triggered by West Berlin disco bombing. Gaddafi survived. One US plane lost. Adopted daughter Hana reportedly killed (disputed). All core details correct.

title: Chad Defeats Libyan Forces in Toyota War
reason: Confirmed: 1987 Toyota War saw Chadian forces with French MILAN anti-tank missiles defeat Libyan armored columns. Libya lost an estimated 7,500 men and $1.5 billion in equipment. Ended effective Libyan military presence in northern Chad. All details correct.

title: Lockerbie Bombing Destroys Pan Am Flight 103
reason: Confirmed: Pan Am Flight 103 exploded over Lockerbie, Scotland on December 21, 1988. All 259 aboard and 11 on the ground killed (270 total). Semtex bomb in cargo. Libyan intelligence eventually identified. All details correct.

title: UTA Flight 772 Bombing
reason: Confirmed: UTA Flight 772 exploded over Niger on September 19, 1989, killing all 170 aboard. Suitcase bomb in cargo hold. French investigation linked to Libyan intelligence; six Libyans convicted in absentia 1999. All details correct.

title: Arab Maghreb Union Founded
reason: Confirmed: Arab Maghreb Union established by Treaty of Marrakesh on February 17, 1989. Members: Algeria, Libya, Mauritania, Morocco, Tunisia. All five countries confirmed. AMU largely inactive due to Morocco-Algeria disputes. All details correct.

title: UN Sanctions Imposed on Libya
reason: Confirmed: UN Security Council Resolution 748 adopted March 31, 1992 imposed sanctions on Libya for refusing to surrender Lockerbie suspects. Aviation ban, arms embargo, reduced diplomacy. All details correct.

title: Libyan Withdrawal from Aouzou Strip
reason: Confirmed: ICJ ruled February 3, 1994 in favor of Chad. Withdrawal began April 15, 1994 and completed May 30, 1994. UN observers present. All details correct.

title: Abu Salim Prison Massacre
reason: Confirmed: June 28-29, 1996, approximately 1,270 prisoners killed at Abu Salim prison following a protest over conditions. Islamist political prisoners were majority of victims. Regime concealed massacre for years. All details correct.

title: Lockerbie Suspects Surrendered for Trial
reason: Confirmed: Megrahi and Fhimah surrendered April 5, 1999 at Camp Zeist, Netherlands. Trial before Scottish judges with no jury. UN sanctions immediately suspended upon handover. All details correct.

title: UN Sanctions Suspended
reason: Confirmed: UN Security Council suspended (not formally lifted) sanctions in April 1999 following Lockerbie suspects' surrender. Air travel resumed. Sanctions fully lifted only in September 2003. Core facts correct.

title: Megrahi Convicted, Fhimah Acquitted
reason: FALSE: Year is wrong. The verdict was delivered January 31, 2001, not 2000. The trial began May 3, 2000 but the verdict came in 2001. Megrahi convicted, Fhimah acquitted — the outcome is correct but the year is off by one.

title: Secret WMD Negotiations Begin
reason: Confirmed: CIA and MI6 began cooperating with Libyan intelligence in 2002. Formal secret negotiations launched in March 2003 when Saif al-Islam contacted MI6. 18-month negotiation period referenced in event is slightly telescoped but essentially correct.

title: Libya Accepts Responsibility for Lockerbie
reason: Confirmed: August 15, 2003, Libya's UN ambassador submitted letter accepting responsibility for Lockerbie. $2.7 billion compensation agreed ($10 million per family). Agreement paved way for UN sanctions lifting. All core details correct.

title: WMD Dismantlement Announced
reason: Confirmed: December 19, 2003, Libya announced voluntary dismantlement of WMD programs. A.Q. Khan network connection confirmed. IAEA verified; equipment airlifted to Oak Ridge, TN. All details correct.

title: US Restores Full Diplomatic Relations with Libya
reason: Confirmed: US Interest Section reopened February 2004, sanctions lifted April-September 2004. Full embassy status achieved May 31, 2006. Description of staged normalization 2004-2006 is accurate. All core facts verified.

title: European Energy Investment Boom Begins
reason: Confirmed: Following 2004 normalization, Libya released EPSA-4 model agreement inviting international oil companies. ENI, Shell, Total, ExxonMobil, BP, ConocoPhillips, and others all signed agreements. All details correct.

title: US Removes Libya from Terrorism Sponsor List
reason: Confirmed: Secretary Rice announced rescission on May 15, 2006; formally completed June 30, 2006. Enabled full diplomatic and military cooperation. All details correct.

title: US-Libya Comprehensive Claims Settlement
reason: Confirmed: Libya paid $1.5 billion into US fund October 2008. Covered Lockerbie, Berlin disco bombing (1986), and Libyan victims of US 1980s airstrikes. Total fund $1.8 billion. All details correct.

title: February 17 Revolution Erupts in Benghazi
reason: Confirmed: Protests began February 15 (not 17) with the Day of Rage officially February 17. Date chosen to commemorate 2006 consulate killings is confirmed. Security forces fired on protesters, east Libya fell under rebel control. Minor note: protests actually started Feb 15 before the Feb 17 'Day of Rage'.

title: NATO Intervention and No-Fly Zone
reason: Confirmed: UNSC Resolution 1973 passed March 17, 2011. NATO Operation Unified Protector launched March 31, ended October 31, 2011. Qatar and UAE involvement confirmed. All details correct.

title: National Transitional Council Established
reason: Confirmed: NTC announced in Benghazi on February 27, 2011. France first to recognize on March 10, 2011. Composed of defected officials and opposition figures. All details correct.

title: Fall of Tripoli and Gaddafi's Death
reason: Confirmed: Tripoli fell August 2011. Gaddafi captured October 20, 2011 in Sirte, hiding in a drainage pipe. Killed shortly after capture, circumstances disputed (suggested summary execution). Death filmed globally. All details correct.

title: First Libyan Elections Since Independence
reason: Confirmed: GNC elections held July 7, 2012 (not described as 'July 2012' which is correct). First free elections since 1952. Moderate nationalist NFA won more seats than Islamist parties. International observers declared broadly free and fair. All details correct.

title: Benghazi US Consulate Attack Kills Ambassador
reason: Confirmed: September 11, 2012, Ansar al-Sharia attacked US mission in Benghazi, killing Ambassador Christopher Stevens and three other Americans (Sean Smith, Tyrone Woods, Glen Doherty). Later characterized as premeditated terrorist attack. All details correct.

title: Political Isolation Law Excludes Former Regime Officials
reason: Confirmed: GNC passed Political Isolation Law in May 2013, passed 164-4 under militia pressure (militias besieged justice and foreign ministries). Banned Gaddafi-era officials for 10 years. All details correct.

title: Oil Production Disruptions Begin
reason: Confirmed: Ibrahim Jathran-led Petroleum Facilities Guard blockaded eastern oil terminals from late July 2013. Production dropped from 1.4 million bpd to approximately 250,000 bpd. Lost revenues estimated at $14 billion. All details correct.

title: Prime Minister Ali Zeidan Kidnapped
reason: Confirmed: PM Ali Zeidan kidnapped early morning October 10, 2013 from Corinthia Hotel in Tripoli by the Operations Room militia. Released hours later. All details correct.

title: Libya Descends into Civil War
reason: Confirmed: Civil war began in 2014. Libya Dawn coalition seized Tripoli, reinstated GNC. Internationally recognized HoR relocated to Tobruk and aligned with Haftar's LNA. Dual government structure confirmed. All details correct.

title: Khalifa Haftar Launches Operation Dignity
reason: Confirmed: Haftar launched Operation Dignity on May 16, 2014, with air strikes against Islamist militias in Benghazi. Called for GNC dissolution. Tobruk government eventually recognized his command. All details correct.

title: ISIS Establishes Presence in Libya
reason: Confirmed: ISIS formally announced presence in Sirte in early 2015, declared it Libyan capital. Controlled approximately 150-250 km of coastline. Attracted Tunisian, Egyptian and other foreign fighters. All core details correct.

title: Libyan Political Agreement and Government of National Accord
reason: Confirmed: Libyan Political Agreement signed December 17, 2015 in Skhirat, Morocco. Created GNA under Fayez al-Sarraj. UN recognized as legitimate government. Haftar's LNA and others refused to accept. GNA entered Tripoli March 2016. All details correct.

title: ISIS Defeated in Sirte
reason: Confirmed: Operation Bunyan Marsous (Impenetrable Wall) cleared ISIS from Sirte. US conducted 495 airstrikes under Operation Odyssey Lightning. GNA declared liberation December 18, 2016. US AFRICOM concluded operation December 19, 2016. All details correct.

title: Haftar's LNA Consolidates Eastern Libya
reason: Confirmed: Haftar declared full control of Benghazi in July 2017 after three-year campaign. UAE, Egypt, and Russia provided critical support. LNA controlled Cyrenaica region. All details correct.

title: Migration Crisis Through Libya Peaks
reason: Confirmed: CNN published undercover footage of migrant slave auctions in November 2017. Libya was primary Mediterranean crossing route. EU-funded Libyan Coast Guard interceptions documented. Reports of slavery and abuse confirmed. All details correct.

title: Haftar Launches Offensive on Tripoli
reason: Confirmed: Haftar launched offensive on April 4, 2019. UN Secretary-General Guterres was in Tripoli when offensive began. LNA advanced to outskirts before being halted. All details correct.

title: Turkey-Libya Maritime and Military Agreement Signed
reason: Confirmed: GNA and Turkey signed maritime boundary and military cooperation MoU on November 27, 2019. Contested by Greece and Cyprus as illegal. Beginning of significant Turkish military engagement. All details correct.

title: Berlin Conference on Libya
reason: Confirmed: Berlin Conference held January 19, 2020. Participants included Russia, Turkey, UAE, Egypt, France, US, and others. Endorsed ceasefire and arms embargo commitments. Agreements were subsequently violated by multiple parties. All details correct.

title: Turkish Military Intervention Reverses Haftar
reason: Confirmed: Turkey deployed military forces, Bayraktar TB2 drones, and Syrian mercenaries (18,000 sent by September 2020). TB2 drones proved devastatingly effective against LNA armor. Haftar's Tripoli offensive reversed. All details correct.

title: October Ceasefire Agreement
reason: Confirmed: Permanent ceasefire signed October 23, 2020, mediated by Stephanie Williams (UN Acting SRSG). GNA and LNA military representatives signed in Geneva. Held with surprising durability. All details correct.

title: Oil Blockade Lifted After Eight Months
reason: Confirmed: Haftar agreed to lift oil blockade September 18, 2020. Blockade had been in place since January 2020. Production recovered to over 1.2 million bpd within months. All details correct.

title: Government of National Unity Formed
reason: Confirmed: LPDF selected Abdul Hamid Dbeibeh as PM on February 5, 2021. Mohamed al-Menfi as Presidency Council head. HoR approved cabinet March 10, 2021. Dbeibeh described as Misratan businessman is correct. All details correct.

title: Presidential Elections Planned but Postponed
reason: Confirmed: December 24, 2021 elections postponed indefinitely. Disputes over electoral laws and candidate eligibility (Haftar and Saif al-Islam Gaddafi both had candidacy controversies). Tied to 70th independence anniversary. All details correct.

title: Dual Government Crisis Deepens
reason: Confirmed: HoR appointed Fathi Bashagha as rival PM in February 2022 (Government of National Stability installed March 2022). Bashagha attempted to enter Tripoli in August 2022 but was repelled by Dbeibeh-aligned militias. All details correct.

title: Derna Flood Disaster Kills Thousands
reason: Confirmed: Storm Daniel caused two dams to fail on September 10-11, 2023. Death toll estimated 4,352 confirmed dead (UN) to 11,300 (initial UN estimate later revised), with 8,000 missing. Infrastructure neglect and governance failures confirmed. Libya's worst modern natural disaster. All core facts correct.

title: Tripoli Militia Violence Resurges
reason: Confirmed: Major fighting erupted in Tripoli on August 14-15, 2023, between Special Deterrence Force (RADA) and 444th Combat Brigade. At least 45 killed, 146 injured. Airport closed. Deadliest Tripoli clashes of 2023. All details correct.

title: Central Bank Governor Crisis and Fuel Shortages
reason: Confirmed: 2024 crisis over replacement of CBL governor Sadiq al-Kabir. LNA-aligned forces shut down over half of oil production (700,000 bpd) in August 2024. al-Kabir fled the country. Fuel shortages confirmed. All details correct.

title: Migration Crisis Continues Through Libya
reason: Libya remained primary Mediterranean transit country through 2024. EU-funded Coast Guard interceptions ongoing. Detention facility abuse reports continued. Migration as diplomatic leverage for Libyan factions is well-documented.
